overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair may limit public participation, and the complainant was allowed to speak later in the meeting. Payroll, budget, procurement, and school committee issues were declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Select Board did not allow public participation at its November 15, 2022 meeting, when the chair stopped the complainant from speaking on Town Manager candidates during the first comment period.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, because it is within the Chair’s discretion to limit public participation during a meeting, the Chair did not violate the Open Meeting Law by preventing the complainant from addressing the Board during the November 15 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised payroll or budget fraud and procurement issues, which were outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: The Division of Open Government is charged specifically with reviewing complaints to determine compliance with the Open Meeting Law , G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, thus we decline to review, and offer no opinion on issues of payroll or budget fraud, or procurement raised in the complaint or request for further review.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised potential issues involving the school committee, but it was only filed with the Select Board and so could not be reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: because the complaint at issue here was only filed with the Select Board, we decline to review any potential issues involving the school committee.
